topic: Receipt Gating and Implied Completion Prohibition (I10)
evidence: I10 (RECEIPTS ARE OPERATIONAL ARTIFACTS): every non-trivial execution writes a receipt. Implied completion prohibited — an agent cannot claim a task is done without a receipt. This prevents the false_completion failure mode (Instinct Pattern 1 precursor). Receipt is the only valid signal of completion. Receipt chain integrity enforced by Guard via required_receipts in state.json. InferenceGuard writes receipt on every execution including non-activations — because absence of activation is itself an operational fact, not a non-event. Module-build tasks cannot be marked complete without acceptance_verified: true in execution-receipt (Executor post-wave gate). Archive is the only module that may declare a task fully complete — it writes the delivery receipt. No module may signal Archive completion on behalf of another module.
